hook: 184 Hittite tablets unearthed in 2026 reveal a dead princess.

sections.voiceover: 184 Hittite tablets unearthed in 2026 reveal a dead princess.
sections.visual_cue: Pile of 184 ancient tablets on a desert floor.

sections.voiceover: 2026 digs at Kayalıpınar, Turkey uncovered 131 tablets, adding to 53 for 184 total. They date to King Tudhaliya II, about 3,400 years ago. What fever killed a princess and why?
sections.visual_cue: Map of Turkey zooming to Kayalıpınar site, then tablets stacked.

sections.voiceover: But the tablets also expose a crisis that threatened the empire’s food supply.
sections.visual_cue: Close‑up of a tablet showing grain ledger with red marks.

sections.voiceover: The tablets record a high‑fever epidemic that killed a royal princess. They list grain rations and livestock loans, showing a strained economy. The 184‑tablet archive reveals religion, disease, and daily life in the Hittite Empire.
sections.visual_cue: Pages of tablets displaying epidemic text and economic tables.

sections.voiceover: 184 tablets now illuminate a forgotten Hittite world.
sections.visual_cue: Zoom on the number 184 etched on a tablet.
